about: The literals a delayexpr may join an integer to, read as the unit the
A delayexpr of the form <integer> + '<literal>' spells the integer's
decimal digits followed by the literal. When the literal, ASCII
whitespace after it aside, is a unit the CSS2 time reader takes ('ms' or
's', either case; ARCHITECTURE.md, 'Durations (Single Source of Truth)'),
the text is a time exactly when the integer is not negative and its
milliseconds fit the largest delay, so the build computes the delay from
the integer with no text in between. Any other literal is read as the
text it joins: a space before the unit, digits, a fraction or another
word would make the join's text something else than the count's time.
Each case gives 'literal' and 'unit': 'ms', 's', or null when the build
reads the join as a text. The build's reading of a literal
(sce-build/src/forge/delay_count.rs) is held to this table, and the Rust
runtime holds its reading of a count (helpers::send::delay_of_count)
equal to its reading of the text over each literal with a unit, for
every value of every integer type.
